video_title: TOP 5 Decks in Clash Royale for the New Meta

clock 1:53-1:47 (t=875-878): deliberately withheld as the answer to the defence rather than as a speed-up — "let's go for the Giant here and then we can go for the Rage once he goes for the Skeleton Army".

giant: clock 1:12 (t=795): played as the pocket tank for extra king-tower damage rather than as the lane opener — "I think we just giant the pocket. Try to grab extra king" (the push then lost value to a lag spike: "Bro, the lag. Oh my god. Okay, at least we grabbed a Sparky shot").

clock 0:03-1:53 (t=866-874): the overtime plan is Giant first, Evo E-Barbs behind — "we can just go for a Giant Evo E Barbs in the pocket", then "Okay, let's go for the Giant here and then we can go for the Rage once he goes for the Skeleton Army".

In this Giant/Sparky/E-Barbs list the Giant is support for the Elite Barbarians, not the win condition: four plays (t=776.1, 814.3, 824.5, 871.9) and only 4 commentary mentions against 13 for the Elite Barbarians.

clock 1:25 (t=901-905): he pre-places Valkyrie for it — "Let's Valkyrie on top as well cuz he's probably going to try to go for the Knight" — and dismisses it again at 942-944s: "He might even knight in the middle but that's not going to work".
ice-spirit: clock 1:09 (t=918-921): the opponent's last-ditch save on a tower already broken by Evo E-Barbs and Minions — "Spirit's going to save him, but it's not going to save him well enough. He's already at 500 HP".

bullets: Deck 5 of 5 in a deck-showcase video; Ryley introduces it at t=696 as "this a giant Sparky e-barbs deck" and immediately editorialises: "I can't believe this is actually viable. It is so sad that, you know, this is what the game has actually come to" (699-712s). Evolutions in play are Evo Elite Barbarians and Evo Wizard.

Stated game plan for a Log Bait matchup, clock 2:15-2:11: "I just need to get a lot of elixir up and just spam my e-barbs cuz I assume he has inferno tower, and I'm not actually going to be able to reset that inferno tower" — the list has no stun and no cheap cycle, so it plays for elixir volume rather than for a reset.

Regulation is a tower trade: a bridge Elite Barbarians + Giant + Rage push takes the enemy left tower 4738 -> 640 HP at clock 1:25-1:17 ("That's just tower down, no matter what he wants", 787-790s), while the opponent's counter leaves Ryley's right tower on 125 HP at clock 1:17.

From triple elixir onward the deck's back-line placements are used as pure denial rather than offence: Sparky at [8, 0] three times, Valkyrie held for the Goblin Barrel/Skarmy pocket, Wizard in the middle — "we're just not letting him attack at all. This is kind of funny. He can't go in" (884-888s).

The game goes to overtime (clock resets at t=868) and the deck closes it in the pocket, not at the bridge: Evo E-Barbs at tile [8, 19] plus Rage at [8, 23] plus Minions at [8, 21] take the enemy right tower 3122 -> 588 HP over clock 1:21-1:03, then Rage and Arrows clear the Skeleton Army at clock 0:42-0:38 — "beautiful arrows just grabbing that skarmy army and that is good game" (948-951s). Win.

new_deck.rationale: Giant plus Sparky with Rage support is a heavy, elixir-hungry push deck that wins in double and triple elixir, with Evolved Elite Barbarians providing the bridge pressure that fills the gap while elixir is banked.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck banks elixir behind Wizard and Valkyrie defences and then commits everything to one lane: Giant in front, Evolved Elite Barbarians beside the tower, Rage on top. Rage is the glue — it is never used to open a push, only dropped on one that has already connected, which is what turns a Skeleton Army block into tower damage. Arrows is the deck's only other spell and does two jobs Ryley names explicitly: killing the Princess he cannot otherwise reach, and clearing the Skarmy on the closing push. The weakness he states himself is that the list carries no stun, so a defensive Inferno Tower cannot be reset and the answer is simply to out-elixir it. Sparky is played almost entirely as a defensive anchor in the back rather than as a win condition.
